column2: Your AI Agent Can Be Compromised. You'd Never Know.
column6: Fetched. Gray Swan write-up of the 2026 UK AISI/US CAISI/Gray Swan indirect-prompt-injection competition (464 participants, 272k attempts, 13 models). Reports named per-model ASRs (Claude Opus 4.5 0.5% to Gemini 2.5 Pro 8.5%; transfer 44-81%) absent from the anonymised NIST/arXiv primary; enters per protocol §5 finding-nowhere-else. Maps to JOINT-2026-03. Pre-cutoff.

column2: UK AISI × Gray Swan Agent Red-Teaming Challenge: Results Snapshot

column2: AgentHarm: A Benchmark for Measuring Harmfulness of LLM Agents (blog)

column2: Comparing AI Agents to Cybersecurity Professionals In Real-World Penetration Testing
column6: Fetched. Original Gray Swan research (ARTEMIS; authors incl. Gray Swan's E. K. Jones): first head-to-head of AI agents vs professional penetration testers on a live enterprise network, finding agents outperform 90% of human professionals. Qualifying empirical finding; not in known_reports. Pre-cutoff.

column2: D-REX: A Benchmark For Detecting Deceptive Reasoning In Large Language Models
column6: Fetched. Gray Swan benchmark (authors incl. Andy Zou, Dan Hendrycks, Zico Kolter, Matt Fredrikson) targeting models that produce benign-appearing outputs from malicious internal reasoning; qualifying methodology/tooling+empirical finding by in-scope evaluator. Not in known_reports. Pre-cutoff.

column2: AgentHarm: A Benchmark for Measuring Harmfulness of LLM Agents

column2: Improving Alignment and Robustness with Circuit Breakers

column2: The WMDP Benchmark: Measuring and Reducing Malicious Use with Unlearning
column6: Fetched. Gray Swan-hosted benchmark (authors incl. N. Li, A. Pan, D. Hendrycks) measuring hazardous knowledge in LLMs and the RMU unlearning method; qualifying methodology+empirical finding by in-scope evaluator. Not in known_reports. Pre-cutoff.
